understand.concept: Standard headers group declarations by responsibility: stdio.h for streams, stdlib.h for general utilities and allocation, string.h for byte/string operations, math.h for mathematics, ctype.h for character classification, time.h for calendar time and stdint.h for integer types.
understand.whyItMatters: Knowing header boundaries makes code easier to navigate and avoids missing declarations or relying on accidental transitive includes.
understand.analogy: Treat a reference or learning task as a contract that states what is expected and how success is checked.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the exact C standard or library specification.

explain.narrative:
Standard headers group declarations by responsibility: stdio.h for streams, stdlib.h for general utilities and allocation, string.h for byte/string operations, math.h for mathematics, ctype.h for character classification, time.h for calendar time and stdint.h for integer types.

Use authoritative declarations and documentation, state assumptions explicitly and verify behaviour with focused examples. Where the implementation or C version matters, record it.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: Each header provides declarations for a distinct responsibility: stdlib.h provides allocation and status macros, string.h provides memcpy, and stdio.h provides puts.

practise.guidedTask: Map each function in the example to its declaring header.
practise.independentTask: Review a source file's includes and add the direct standard header for every library facility it uses.
hints: Include the header that declares a function instead of relying on another header to include it indirectly.
Avoid unnecessary headers that obscure module dependencies.
A header supplies declarations; the implementation supplies the library behaviour.
